newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tackle EU jobs problem, top Japanese banker urges.
newsitem.headline: Tackle EU jobs problem, top Japanese banker urges.

text.p: A top Japanese banker on Tuesday urged EU states to tackle the region's stubborn unemployment problem in the run-up to monetary union.

Industrial Bank of Japan chairman Yoh Kurosawa told the Global 24 monetary union conference that Japanese investors were interested in investment in the euro bloc but did not see the euro as competing with the yen.
Speaking on a video link from Tokyo, Kurosawa said: "We Japanese welcome very much a strong Europe, a strong European currency."
But he added: "We all know that European countries are suffering from unemployment and I think this is the first target."
Kurosawa said Japanese investors were on the lookout for buying opportunities amid record low interest rates at home.
Traditionally, they had bought U.S., New Zealand and Australian bonds, but the yen had appreciated against those currencies in the past three weeks, he said.
"If you have a huge euro bond market that would be an opportunity for investment. We welcome that opportunity."
But he also said that the Japanese business community did not expect the euro to compete with the Japanese yen after it is launched in January 1999, as currently planned.
"We don't see any sense in which the euro would be competing with the Japanese yen," he said.
